title.narrative: Overall Goal: To contribute to the reduction of child labour, particularly its worst forms in agricultural sector in Chipata and Nkeyema District of Zambia.

description.narrative: The Action responds to the call of the National Action Plan 2015 on Child Labour (NAPCL) for multisector direction to child labour. The Action will improve the protection of children, notably children (5 17 years) in hazardous and worst form of child labour (WFCL) in tobacco growing communities through: Increased access to education and vocational skill training, triggered by withdrawing children from child labour, rehabilitating, preventing and reintegrating them into education and skills training including establishing a conducive living environment in schools for children; increased access to income for economic livelihood and food security of vulnerable households; Increased awareness on child labour and rights of children; Increased labour inspection and enforcement of labour laws and regulations; enhanced technical knowledge, monitoring and coordination mechanisms of district stakeholders to address child labour and citizens empowered to lobby for improvements in the provision of education and protection of children in hazardous work including those in WFCL and children trafficked

title.narrative: Specific Objective 2: To enhance the capacity of Government structures and CSOs to address child labour through the scale up of withdraw, rehabilitation, reintegration, coordination, regulatory and policy commitment.

description.narrative: The Action will increase the overall capacity of National and District stakeholders to address child labour using an integrated Area Based Approach which mobilises stakeholders/partners and pools resources for implementation of child labour programmes. This increased capacity will be acquired through: training of national and district stakeholders on child labour protocols and Occupation Safety and Health (OSH) based on a skills gap/capacity assessment; the strengthening of district Child Labour Monitoring Systems (CLMS), the drafting and implementation of robust multisectoral plans including mainstreaming of child labour programmes sectoral plans in the two target districts to build community capacities to respond to child labour challenges, and the enhancement of national and district coordination and learning mechanisms; effective social accountability at community/district level and escalation of child labour issues at province/national levels; improved economic livelihood of families and communities cushioning them against economic shocks and food insecurity. This will lead to strengthened implementation of the NAPCL which this Action is championing

title.narrative: Intermediate Outcomes 2.2: Improved economic livelihoods of families and communities cushioning them against economic shocks and food insecurity.

description.narrative: The Action will target 1,802 households and increase household capacity to expand their IGAs/livelihoods through Self Help Group (community saving scheme); produce and utilise locally available nutrient crops, and to rear and produce small livestock (mostly goats) as part of IGAs and food security. This will lead to improvements in the households income and food security, notably by families with children withdrawn or prevented from child labour. The trainings on agricultural production and livestock rearing will allow the farmers to start some income generation activities, with a positive impact on household income and food security. The Action will also increase the beneficiaries access to communitybased loan facilities (cash via SelfHelp Groups and pass on loan schemes for small livestock) which will generate capital to invest in education for children and food security.
